title: Retail Inventory Batch Processing with Dataproc
business: Large-scale retail enterprises managing massive daily transaction logs across thousands of physical store locations.
problem: Legacy on-premises Hadoop clusters struggle with rigid capacity constraints, leading to delayed inventory reconciliation and stock-out risks during peak shopping seasons.
solution: Google Cloud Dataproc provides a managed environment to run Spark and Hadoop jobs, allowing the retailer to decouple storage from compute and dynamically scale clusters based on the volume of daily transaction logs.
steps: Provision a Dataproc cluster using managed Spark and Hadoop components.
Configure Cloud Storage as the primary data lake to store raw transaction logs.
Submit Spark jobs to the cluster to perform distributed aggregation and inventory reconciliation.
Scale the cluster worker nodes horizontally to handle spikes in transaction volume.
Terminate the cluster after job completion to optimize resource utilization.
outcome: The retailer achieves faster inventory insights and consistent processing times regardless of daily transaction volume, without maintaining permanent hardware.
limitation: Dataproc clusters incur costs while running; users must monitor cluster uptime and job scheduling to avoid unnecessary expenses, which can be checked via Cloud Billing reports.
